title: No zeroize on drop for key material
description: Affects all key-handling code across the codebase. The zeroize crate is not used anywhere. Specific instances: (1) federation.rs:540-542 — RSA private key parsed from PEM and used for signing, then dropped without zeroing. (2) push.rs:65-68 — VAPID SigningKey generated and serialized to PEM, original key object dropped without zeroing. (3) push.rs:347-356 — ECDH EphemeralSecret and shared_secret.raw_secret_bytes() IKM dropped without zeroing. (4) push.rs:379 — CEK (content encryption key) stored in [u8; 16] on stack, dropped without zeroing. (5) did.rs:4-10 — Ed25519 SigningKey and private key bytes returned as plain [u8; 32], dropped without zeroing. (6) push.rs:366-368 — HKDF-derived ikm_derived [u8; 32] dropped without zeroing. Impact: keys persist in freed heap/stack memory and could be recovered via memory dumps, core dumps, or swap. Add zeroize dep, use Zeroizing<T> wrapper or implement ZeroizeOnDrop for types holding key material.
